name: Claude Code
summary: Anthropic's terminal-native coding agent for large repositories, MCP-connected tools, skills, hooks, and team workflows.
overview: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-native coding agent for working inside software projects. The page should explain it as an agentic engineering environment: repository context, CLAUDE.md memory, slash commands, skills, hooks, MCP connectors, and permission settings all shape how it behaves. It is a core Agent category because many reusable skills, command packs, and MCP integrations are designed around Claude Code first.

strengths.title: Large-codebase navigation
strengths.body: A strong fit when the agent must understand project structure, modify files, and reason across a long-running coding session.

strengths.title: MCP-connected tool use
strengths.body: Claude Code documents MCP as a first-class way to connect external tools, prompts, authenticated services, and data sources.

strengths.title: Reusable workflow surfaces
strengths.body: Slash commands, skills, hooks, subagents, and plugins give teams several ways to package repeatable engineering behavior.

strengths.title: Project memory near the code
strengths.body: CLAUDE.md and related memory patterns let teams keep conventions, architecture notes, and operating rules close to the repository.

extensionModel.label: MCP
extensionModel.body: MCP is a central integration layer for tools, prompts, and external services in Claude Code.

extensionModel.label: Skills
extensionModel.body: Skills are suitable for comprehensive reusable capabilities with structure, scripts, references, and team workflows.

extensionModel.label: Hooks
extensionModel.body: Hooks let teams intercept and control agent behavior around tool use, notifications, validation, and workflow automation.

extensionModel.label: Workflow
extensionModel.body: Custom commands and skills are good for PR review, lint repair, migration routines, release checks, and operational checklists.

recommendedStacks.title: Team repository assistant
recommendedStacks.body: Combine Claude Code with project memory, skills, and code-review workflows for shared engineering standards.

recommendedStacks.title: MCP-connected engineering loop
recommendedStacks.body: Use MCP-backed GitHub, docs, issue tracker, database, or observability tools when implementation depends on external systems.

recommendedStacks.title: Command and skill library
recommendedStacks.body: Treat Claude Code as a reference ecosystem for slash commands and structured skills that other agents may later adapt.

limitations: MCP servers, hooks, plugins, and commands can reach sensitive systems, so permissions and source review matter.
Teams should document who owns shared commands and skills; otherwise the workflow layer becomes hard to audit.
Do not collapse Claude Code skills, slash commands, hooks, and MCP into one generic extension label.
Community packages should remain candidate-only until their source, maintenance, and scope are reviewed.
